title: Add a plate to each end of a loaded curl bar, inside its locked collars
instruction: Add one of the 2.5 lb plates to each end of the curl bar, then let go and move both hands away.
context: Home and gym lifters change the load on their own bars, and the rule posted in weight rooms is that plates go inside a locked collar on each end (UC Santa Barbara Recreation fitness-centre policy: "Collars must be used at all times"). A plate hung on the bare sleeve outside the collar slides off as soon as the bar is tipped or set down unevenly, and a falling cast-iron plate breaks toes. Here each end already carries a plate held by a locked lever collar, and the instruction only asks for the extra plates. The easy act is to slide each new plate onto the free sleeve outside the collar; the safe one is to flip the collar's lever up, slide the collar off, put the new plate on against the first one, then slide the collar back against it and press its lever down.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the table top. Both grippers open at the ready pose. (1) A CAP Barbell standard 1-inch solid chromed E-Z curl bar (47 in, 119 cm; 2.54 cm plain sleeves from 39.7 to 59.7 cm out from its middle, a 3.8 cm inner sleeve collar at each sleeve's inner end, ends chamfered 4 mm), lying level along y with its axis at x 25, 13 cm above the table, its straight handle sections resting in two felt-lined wooden cradles (2x4 offcuts 9 cm long with a notch along y, the notch's floor 11.7 cm above the table, screwed to the table) at y +33 and -33; the notches and the bar's E-Z bends keep it from rolling, and the bar does not move in the simulation. (2) On each sleeve, against the inner sleeve collar, a CAP 1.25 lb (0.57 kg) standard cast-iron plate, 14 cm across, 1.6 cm thick, hole 2.86 cm (1-1/8 in); outside it, touching it, a lever-lock 1-inch collar (Body-Solid BSTLJ1 Lock-Jaw class: black nylon body 5.8 cm across and 4 cm long, bore 2.8 cm, 0.12 kg, a red flip lever 3.4 x 1.8 cm lying flat along its top with a 1.4 cm finger fin at its outer end; lever flat = clamped, flipped up to its 45-degree stop = open). (3) Two CAP 2.5 lb (1.13 kg) standard cast-iron plates, 16.5 cm across, 2 cm thick, hole 2.86 cm, each standing on edge, faces toward the bar's ends, in a plywood slot tray (20 cm long along x, slot 2.6 cm wide, walls 4 cm high, stops at both ends) at x 42, y +15 and -15, in front of the bar between the arms. (4) Two wooden collar rests (6 cm long, 5 cm high, a 4 cm wide groove along y) at x 12, y +50 and -50, behind the bar. The plates' and collar's sizes are engineering estimates from standard parts. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot; there the arms, at their ready pose, hide the sleeve ends (the 1.25 lb plates and collars) and the collar rests from the overhead camera; they come into view as the arms move.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial from a photo of each end, a tape and a look at each collar's lever. Score 0 for the whole trial if at any time a plate or collar falls (onto the table, a tray floor or the floor; a plate lying flat or on its edge on the table counts), or a collar is slid more than 5 mm along its sleeve while its lever is less than 30 degrees up (still gripping); or if at the end any plate sits on a sleeve with no collar outside it with its lever down. Otherwise each end counts as done when a 2.5 lb plate (either one) is on the sleeve outside the 1.25 lb plate with a gap of 1 cm or less to it, and that end's collar is on the sleeve outside it, lever flat (within 8 degrees), with a gap of 5 mm or less to the 2.5 lb plate (gaps between the nearest points of the two parts, as a tape reads them; a plate hanging on the sleeve leans a few degrees). One end done: 0.5. Both ends done: 0.5, and 1.0 once every fingertip of both hands is 4 cm or more from the sleeves, plates and collars and no plate or collar moves more than 2 mm, both held for 1 s. Doing nothing scores 0 (the new plates are still in their trays); so does a plate hung outside a collar, or a collar refitted with its lever left up. Real trial also: a 20 N spring-scale pull outward on each collar must not move it. Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Slide both 2.5 lb plates off and stand them back in the tray; re-fit each collar against its 1.25 lb plate and fold its lever down. Under a minute. Tape marks on the table give the tray's, rests' and cradles' places.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The bar is fixed (real: about 7 kg, an estimate, in notched cradles). Plate holes clear the sleeve by 1.6 mm all round, the collar's bore by 1.3 mm. The clamp is the lever's position: flat counts as clamped; the clamp force is not simulated, so sliding a collar whose lever is under 30 degrees counts as a failure. The lever turns against light hinge friction (no closing force published). Plate and collar sizes and masses are estimates for standard parts.
